info.description:
Integrator-facing REST surface of the setjoin on-premise mail server.

SCOPE: this spec is the phased integrator and administrator contract. It
includes auth, JMAP discovery, broad gateway coverage, and the complete
exact-method Setjoin Drive surface; remaining debt is explicit in the ledger.
Coverage is fenced by
`scripts/check-openapi-coverage.sh`: every registered gateway route must be
either documented here or listed in `mailserver/api/openapi-pending.txt`
(the coverage-debt ledger), so a new route can never silently ship
undocumented, and a documented path can never reference a dead route. The
Much of the handler layer is still map/anonymous-struct dominated, so most
contracts remain hand-authored while typed DTO generation expands — see
`mailserver/api/AGENTS.md`.

Opens a time-boxed activation window on the caller's eligible assignment
for role `{id}`. Auth: `requireAuth` only (actor = claims.UserID — never
from the request body, DATABASE_SECURITY R2/R3). Returns `activatedUntil`
timestamp. If the token predates the eligible assignment (`IsAdmin=false`
while the user now has an eligible grant), the response includes

deriving admin consoles (D6 cold-start signal).

active window immediately. Auth: `requireAuth` only (self-service).

get.description:
Returns all `approval_requests` where the caller is either the designated
approver (role_group membership or direct user match) or the requester.
Auth: `requireAuth` only (actor = `claims.UserID`, never from request body —
DATABASE_SECURITY R2). All queries run inside `RunUserScoped`, which sets
`app.current_user_id` → FORCE RLS on `approval_requests`.

200.description: The caller's approvals, split into two lists: requests awaiting the caller's decision (`pendingForMe`) and requests the caller submitted (`myRequests`). Each is an array of the same approval-request item.

get.summary: List the caller's approval requests (pending-for-me and submitted)

post.description:
Calls the consumer-specific `*_approval_decide` reducer (`rbac_approval_decide`,
`mail_external_approval_decide`, or `group_moderation_approval_decide`) and
resolves the downstream action. Auth: `requireAuth` only (actor =
`claims.UserID`, never from the request body). RLS gate: only the designated
approver can see + decide the request — a stranger gets opaque 404 (RLS returns
0 rows, no BZ exposed); a requester who can see the row but is not the approver
gets BZ107 → 403. BZ106 → 400 (request not pending). BZ108 → 400 (invalid
decision value). BZ109 → 403 (self-approval not allowed).

capabilities.description: Drive-access approvals only; must be a subset of the request.

expectedEpoch.description: Required when approving a Drive-access request; this is the immutable request-time epoch and stale epochs fail closed.

expiresAt.description: Drive-access approvals only; may not exceed the requested expiry.

maxUses.description: Drive-access approvals only; may not exceed the requested bound.

propagation.description: Drive-access approvals only; may only narrow the request.

204.description: Decision recorded and downstream action resolved

400.description:
`BZ106` — request is not pending (already decided or expired).
`BZ108` — decision value is not `approve` or `deny`.

403.description:
`BZ107` — caller is not the designated approver for this request.
`BZ109` — caller is the requester (self-approval not allowed).

404.description: Request not found (or RLS opaque-404 for a stranger probe)

get.description:
Returns verbatim the access token the caller is already presenting
(session cookie or Bearer). A freshly opened tab holds the shared
session cookie and the persisted binding key but no token string, and
a stale tab holds a string another tab's refresh already rotated away
— both mint inadmissible DPoP proofs with no way back. This read
self-authenticates through the admission-recovery funnel — everything
the regular funnel enforces except the DPoP `ath` claim (a cnf-bound
token still requires a proof bound to its `cnf.jkt`) — so the tab
re-derives its `ath` source without minting or rotating anything and
the other tabs' view of the session is untouched. Not behind
requireAuth deliberately: requireAuth enforces the very `ath` claim a
recovering tab cannot compute yet. Proxied through the gateway's
rate-limited auth proxy.

access_token.description: The exact token string the caller presented.

401.description: Not authenticated — the recovery funnel rejected the presented token/proof.
